result.stdout:
usage: dotnet meta gen [<metadataDir>] --out <dir> [--namespace <ns>] [--generators <a,b,c>] [--template-root <dir>] [--emit-abstract-shapes] [--baseline default|adopt] [--strict]
       dotnet meta gen --list
  runs the generator list in codegen/Generators.cs (`dotnet meta init` writes it);
  --generators narrows that list to the entries named, and never adds one.
  --strict: an unknown @attr is an error (exit 1, nothing written), as in verify (ADR-0023);
  without it gen warns and generates. Owned copies identical to the shipped generators
  get one advisory line naming `dotnet meta eject --undo`.
  column/table naming: "naming" in .metaobjects/config.json (ADR-0058), not a flag here

result.stdout:
usage: dotnet meta eject <name>... [--force] [--root <dir>]
       dotnet meta eject --undo [<name>...] [--force] [--root <dir>]
  --undo drops owned copies identical to the shipped generators (every one, or the names given);
  a copy that differs is refused (exit 2) unless --force. It prints the codegen/Generators.cs edit
  that points the entry back at the shipped generator and never edits the project.
  There is no `doctor` command: gen's notice and `dotnet meta gen --list` show identical or stale copies.
